content: The prevalence of diabetes during pregnancy has been increasing both in the United States and globally, largely in parallel with the obesity epidemic. This trend includes a notable rise in type 2 diabetes among women of reproductive age, as well as an increase in cases of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM). Diabetes during pregnancy poses significant risks to both maternal and fetal health. For the mother, it is associated with complications such as spontaneous abortion, preeclampsia, and preterm delivery. For the fetus, it increases the likelihood of congenital anomalies, macrosomia (excessive fetal growth), neonatal hypoglycemia (low blood sugar levels in the newborn), elevated bilirubin levels (jaundice), and respiratory distress syndrome. Furthermore, diabetes in pregnancy elevates the risk of the mother developing hypertension and type 2 diabetes in the postpartum period. It also increases the likelihood that the offspring will develop diabetes later in life.
